items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
GRCA 2023 Budget Presentation
notes:
Samantha Lawson, Chief Administrative Officer, Grand River Conservation Authority (GRCA) and Sonja Radoja, Manager of Corporate Services GRCA provided a presentation outlining the work of the GRCA, their strategic priorities, and the impacts of Bill 23 on conservation land to support housing development. S. Radoja provided an overview of the GRCA’s 2023 budget noting that they were challenged with managing current inflation pressures, staff restructuring, and record increases in conservation area visits. She highlighted that their operating expenses are up 4.5%, their capital budget is down 10.3%, and the Region’s portion of the general municipal levy is increasing by 3.4%.

Responding to questions, S. Lawson explained that the Bill 23 requirements with respect to the inventory for land to be built on is an internal document. She stressed that disposing of any land involves screening the property against various criteria and that any land that may be suitable for housing will be a small fraction of the land owned by the GRCA. She further noted that they have an intensive program for maintenance and forecasting the capital needs for the major dams.

items.title: Public Hearing of Development Charges Complaint under Subsection 20(4) of the “Development Charges Act”, 1997, as Amended
COR-CFN-23-007, Development Charge Complaint- McLean-Peister Limited, 375 New Dundee Road, Kitchener
notes:
Chair M. Harris provided an overview of the process for the hearing.  

John Doherty, Gowling WLG, provided a presentation on behalf of McLean-Peister. A copy of the presentation is appended to the original minutes. He provided a background of the property and their client’s complaint. He explained that McLean-Peister Limited was charged the non-residential, general services plus water development charges rate for the property, however there was not municipal water services at the property line and McLean-Peister was required to bring water services to the property. He provided an overview of relevant case law and outlined the remedy sought by McLean-Peister.

Richard Brookes, Senior Solicitor, provided an overview of the staff report. He noted that McLean-Peister’s only issue is the credit being sought in regard to the watermain. He explained that the Region’s jurisdiction is over water production while the City of Kitchener has jurisdiction over water distribution. He stressed that the Region’s development charges calculation does not include water distribution only production, which the development is receiving. It is staff’s position that the proper party to this complaint is the City of Kitchener, that the service that is subject to the Region’s development charge is being provided, and that the complaint should be dismissed

J. Doherty was provided with an opportunity to reply noting that their submission was properly made under the Act and ought to be allowed as set out in their submission.

COR-FFM-23-001, King-Victoria Transit Hub Project Update
notes:
Ellen McGaghey, Director, Facilities and Fleet Management provided an update on the King Victoria Transit Hub project and noted that the first phase of the project is for the relocation of the train platforms by Metrolinx. She provided an overview of how the relocation will occur and noted that staff are currently working on an MOU for a cost sharing agreement.

In response to a question from the Committee, E. McGaghey stated that Metrolinx is planning on starting on relocation of services in August 2023.

Responding to questions, Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development & Legislative Services, Planning, Development and Legislative Services, explained that the business community is stressing the importance of transit connectivity to the competitiveness of the regional economy. He further noted that this is a key project in the transit system that will spur additional development and new intensification projects.

In response to a question from the Committee, Craig Dyer, Commissioner, Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer, stated that the estimated cost of phase 2 is in the range of $100 million and that an application was submitted to the Investing in Canada Infrastructure Program and if successful 73% of the funding would be covered with the remaining costs to be financed by the Region.

items.title: PDL-CUL-23-001, Kitchener-Waterloo Symphony One-Time Funding Request
notes:
Helen Chimirri-Russell, Director, Cultural Services, provided an overview of the report noting that it is responding to the request from the Kitchener-Waterloo Symphony for one time funding.

Bruce Lauckner, Chief Administrative Officer, highlighted that the previous Council had directed staff to bring forward a grant program that will be coming forward in a month and noted that there are other organizations that may come forward with other requests for funding outside of the coming grant program. 

In response to a question from the Committee, C. Dyer stated that there is an allocation for grants in the budget, which is $80,000 lower than last year and staff would seek approval of the overall amount in the budget process with allocation to be determined after budget approval. He further noted that the grant process will be discussed further at the Strategic Planning and Budget Committee on February 8, 2023.

The Committee discussed the need to listen to the competing requests for funding and to ground the decision in policy direction from Council.

items.title: PDL-LEG-23-007, Camera-based Traffic Enforcement Programs and Processing Administration
notes:
R. Regier provided an overview of the report noting that the Region is responsible for the administration of the provincial offences act court. Staff are seeking direction to develop an adjudicated case management system to streamline administration, to increase the number of cameras over the next two years, and to develop a road map to include all the school sites across the Region.

Responding to questions, R. Regier stated that staff have had discussions with third party providers regarding the administration of the program, and that staff are planning to bring a report in the next few months on the costs and potential implementation of a Regional processing center. Theresa Mendler, Manager, Strategic Community Planning Initiatives, further explained that there is currently capacity to handle 30,000 charges with the joint processing center in Toronto and that staff believe that it is necessary to begin looking at other options for this processing in the future.  

Mathieu Goetzke, Commissioner, Transportation Services, responded to questions, noting that the Region’s focus for automated speed enforcement has been on school zones but that it would be possible to expand the program to community safety zones. Jeff Schelling, Regional Solicitor, further explained the legislation and process involved in designating a community safety zone.

The Committee recessed at 11:45 a.m. and reconvened at 12:00 p.m.

The Committee discussed the need to expedite the expansion of the automated speed enforcement program; consideration of developing, or partnering on, more processing; identifying solutions for traffic calming in rural areas; and expansion of automated speed enforcement to community safety zones. 

The Committee agreed to amend the motion to include: 
e.    That staff be directed to report back by the second quarter of 2023 with:

a.    a plan for the creation, costing, and funding of a Region of Waterloo processing centre; and
b.    information on potential third party providers of this service;

f.    That staff undertake workshops with Township staff in March and April 2023 to identify specific traffic calming problem statements and implementation of possible solutions, including road redesign, beginning in summer 2023; and
g.    That staff be directed to investigate the expansion of the Automated Speed Enforcement Program to include community safety zones, including to the entire Region.

items.title: Councillor Colleen James Notice of Motion
notes:
C. James introduced her motion noting the importance of community consultation and that this process would improve the opportunity for the Region and the community to provide comments.

The Committee agreed to amend the motion to include ensuring that the police board include the community engagement process in the development of its annual budget prior to presenting its draft annual budget to Regional Council.

motions.item_title: PDL-LEG-23-007, Camera-based Traffic Enforcement Programs and Processing Administration
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions with respect to camera based traffic enforcement programs and processing administration as set out in report PDL-LEG-23-007 dated February 7, 2023: issue a joint Request for Information on behalf of collaborating municipalities for the development and implementation of an adjudicative case management system required for a Regional administrative penalties system; and authorize the Regional Solicitor to establish a Regional administrative penalties system for camera-based offences pursuant to Ontario Regulation 355/22, Administrative Penalties for Contraventions Detected Using Camera Systems , including preparation of the necessary bylaws and agreements with the Province, and to report back on associated staff resources and budget requirements; and direct staff to investigate the feasibility of accelerating the currently planned 2023 Automated Speed Enforcement Program to achieve a total of 32 sites in 2023 and report back to Council in the Spring; and direct staff to present a roadmap for a rapid implementation plan to expand automated speed enforcement to all eligible school locations across the Region, aligned with upcoming strategic planning and 2024 budget planning considerations, including costing for the infrastructure and programming of the camera technology, market capacity to respond, staff resources and budgets and administrative capacity required as well as options for increasing processing capacity.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions with respect to camera based traffic enforcement programs and processing administration as set out in report PDL-LEG-23-007 dated February 7, 2023:

  1. issue a joint Request for Information on behalf of collaborating municipalities for the development and implementation of an adjudicative case management system required for a Regional administrative penalties system; and
  2. authorize the Regional Solicitor to establish a Regional administrative penalties system for camera-based offences pursuant to Ontario Regulation 355/22, Administrative Penalties for Contraventions Detected Using Camera Systems, including preparation of the necessary bylaws and agreements with the Province, and to report back on associated staff resources and budget requirements; and
  3. direct staff to investigate the feasibility of accelerating the currently planned 2023 Automated Speed Enforcement Program to achieve a total of 32 sites in 2023 and report back to Council in the Spring; and
  4. direct staff to present a roadmap for a rapid implementation plan to expand automated speed enforcement to all eligible school locations across the Region, aligned with upcoming strategic planning and 2024 budget planning considerations, including costing for the infrastructure and programming of the camera technology, market capacity to respond, staff resources and budgets and administrative capacity required as well as options for increasing processing capacity.

motions.item_title: Councillor Colleen James Notice of Motion
motions.text: Whereas the Police Budget is the single largest line in the Region of Waterloos operating budget; Whereas the Police Services Act gives the Police Board exclusive authority to decide the detailed composition of the Budget and the Region of Waterloo can only either accept or reject the Police budget in its entirety; And Whereas this budgeting arrangement is best managed between the Board and the Council on a collaborative basis; Whereas the community needs an opportunity to provide input before the budget is finalized; And Whereas it was until recently the practice that the Board and Chief would present their budget to Council prior to the Boards final budget approval; And Whereas this new practice works counter to the preferred collaborative approach; Therefore Be it resolved that the Region of Waterloo Council respectfully request that the Waterloo Regional Police Service Chief of Police: a. return to its past practice and present its draft annual budget to Regional Council, area municipalities, and to the community to allow time for both the Regional Council and the community to review and to provide comments prior to the Waterloo Regional Police Service Board finalizing its annual budget; and b. ensure that a community engagement process be included in the development of the annual budget prior to presenting its draft annual budget to Regional Council
motions.text_html:
Whereas the Police Budget is the single largest line in the Region of Waterloos operating budget;

Whereas the Police Services Act gives the Police Board exclusive authority to decide the detailed composition of the Budget and the Region of Waterloo can only either accept or reject the Police budget in its entirety;

And Whereas this budgeting arrangement is best managed between the Board and the Council on a collaborative basis;

Whereas the community needs an opportunity to provide input before the budget is finalized;

And Whereas it was until recently the practice that the Board and Chief would present their budget to Council prior to the Boards final budget approval;

And Whereas this new practice works counter to the preferred collaborative approach;

Therefore Be it resolved that the Region of Waterloo Council respectfully request that the Waterloo Regional Police Service Chief of Police:

a.  return to its past practice and present its draft annual budget to Regional Council, area municipalities, and to the community to allow time for both the Regional Council and the community to review and to provide comments prior to the Waterloo Regional Police Service Board finalizing its annual budget; and

b.  ensure that a community engagement process be included in the development of the annual budget prior to presenting its draft annual budget to Regional Council
